title: Zombieland Saga Movie: Yumeginga Paradise
content:
Remember the cliffhanger from the end of season two? yeah we’re finally getting some closure.

Zombieland saga has had its fair share of controversy between the fans, but one of the most controversies and the most discussed one in fan circles was always the use of CG in the concert portions of the show, and about that, I would preface this review by saying that this movie redeem all of those criticisms for once and for all.

It is no longer an understatement to say that this movie is the best the show has ever looked. And I am not only talking about the art style oruse of CG. It’s about the cinematography the framing everything comes together to form a high-quality animation production. that’s not to say that CG was not used at all. I mean, let’s be honest. This is a modern show computer assisted animation is the norm but this movie was so subtle with it or rather it blended the to the animation perfectly well with the CG that it’s no longer noticeable which is an achievement when it comes to anime.

Weirdly enough for this franchise, this was an  action heavy movie that did not hold back when it came to music and performing, but the action seemed like it was a priority here more than ever. It felt bigger than life, almost as if it was the entire premise and honestly, it was better for it.

The movie was darker than the rest of the show. It tackled some real horrifying tragedies of a magnitude that the show has never really stepped into all the while being an entertaining family friendly movie that even non-fans and non-anime enjoyers can pick up and enjoy. 

Don’t let the fact that this is a movie distract you into dismissing it under the filler veil. This movie is entirely canon and it continues the story exactly from where season two left off, so in a way for people who seek to put a conclusion on the Zombieland saga franchise. The movie is a must watch.

Overall: 7.8/10.
